nodes.characterization_summary: α-Co(OH)₂ shows clear (003) reflection peak with highest intensity indicating typical intercalation structure with interlayer spacing of 0.78 nm; β-Co(OH)₂ exhibits (100) reflection with narrow interlayer spacing of 0.31 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern of a-Co(OH)₂ shows a clear (003) reflection peak with the highest intensity, indicating a typical intercalation structure with an interlayer spacing of 0.78 nm, while β-Co(OH)₂ exhibits a (100) reflection with a narrow interlayer spacing of 0.31 nm.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both α-Co(OH)₂ and β-Co(OH)₂ exhibit regular hexagonal plate-like structure with adjacent-edge angle of 120° and lateral size of 2-3 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The morphology of the as-prepared α- and β-Co(OH)₂ was studied by scanning electron microscopy (SEM). Both a-Co(OH)₂ and β-Co(OH)₂ exhibit a regular hexagonal plate-like structure with an adjacent-edge angle of 120° and lateral size of 2-3 μm.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM shows lattice fringes of 0.39 nm corresponding to (006) crystal plane of α-phase and 0.27 nm for (110) plane of β-phase. SAED shows well-defined hexagonally arranged spots indicating monocrystalline structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution (HR)TEM images of two Co(OH)₂ nanoplatelets show typical lattice fringes of 0.39 nm for α-Co(OH)₂ (Fig. 1dii) and 0.27 nm for β-Co(OH)₂ (Fig. 1eii), respectively, which correspond to the (006) and (110) crystal planes of the α and β-phase, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping demonstrates uniform distribution of Co and O elements in both α-Co(OH)₂ and β-Co(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, the EDX mapping results further demonstrate the uniform distribution of Co and O elements in a-Co(OH)₂ and β-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: After ECA, α-Co(OH)₂ (003) peak shifts from 11.2° to 13.0° and (006) from 22.4° to 26.0°, indicating phase change similar to γ-CoOOH; β-Co(OH)₂ shows only slight shift.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the ECA process, the (003) reflection of a-Co(OH)₂ shows a right shift from 11.2° to 13.0° along with a reduction in crystallinity. Meanwhile, the (006) peak also shifts to higher angle from 22.4° to 26.0°.

nodes.characterization_summary: α-Co(OH)₂ after ECA shows disappearance of Co-OH at 798 cm⁻¹ and appearance of O-Co-O at 568 cm⁻¹ indicating conversion to CoOOH; β-Co(OH)₂ shows both peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FTIR spectra show that the initial Co–OH bending vibration at 798 cm⁻¹ of E-α-Co(OH)₂ vanishes and an O–Co–O vibration at 568 cm⁻¹ appears, indicating the conversion of Co(OH)₂ to CoOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES of E-α-Co(OH)₂ displays significant right shift of white line to higher binding energy (~5 eV), similar to CoOOH, demonstrating Co valence increase from 2+ to 3+; β-Co(OH)₂ shows little valence change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the white line of E-α-Co(OH)₂ displays a significant right shift to higher binding energy ~5 eV (similar to CoOOH), demonstrating that the valence of Co increases from 2+ to 3+. However, there is little valence change between β-Co(OH)₂ and E-β-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: E-α-Co(OH)₂ shows Co-O and Co-Co peaks shift from 2.10 to 1.90 Å and 3.10 to 2.85 Å indicating Co³⁺-OOH formation; β-Co(OH)₂ shows no change.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the ECA process, the positions of the Co–O and Co–Co peaks shifted significantly (2.10 to 1.90 Å and 3.10 to 2.85 Å, respectively), indicating the formation of Co³⁺-OOH for E-α-Co(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: O 1s XPS shows new O²⁻ peak at 529.5 eV for both E-α-Co(OH)₂ and E-β-Co(OH)₂ after ECA; reversible changes during charge/discharge for α phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both the O1s XPS spectra of E-α-Co(OH)₂ and E-β-Co(OH)₂ show a new peak at 529.5 eV, which is a typical O²⁻ peak, indicating that the ECA process reconstructs the chemical environment of O.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots show initial α- and β-Co(OH)₂ electrodes have similar charge transfer resistance (R_ct). After ECA, E-α-Co(OH)₂ shows obviously improved ion diffusion (decreased resistance) while E-β-Co(OH)₂ shows little improvement.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the Nyquist plots of the EIS spectra show that the initial α- and β-Co(OH)₂ electrodes exhibited similar charge transfer resistance (R_ct). After the ECA process, the ion diffusion with the E-α-Co(OH)₂ electrode is obviously improved, while there is just little improvement for E-β-Co(OH)₂ electrode.
